chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The owner of the commodity is more rightful to bargaining.
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to initiate bargaining in an Islamic sale?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, establishes the seller's priority in initiating price negotiations (sawm), a principle widely cited by Shia jurists to define the procedural ethics of trade. It reflects the Prophetic tradition of ensuring fairness and preventing deception in commercial dealings, reinforcing the seller's authority over the initial valuation of their goods.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, form Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The owner of the commodity is more rightful to (putting) the price tag’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy, who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
The owner of merchandise is more rightful to set up the price for his merchandise.’”
